summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, and a history of anticoagulation was readmitted for worsening shortness of breath, productive cough, and orthopnea. She had been discharged recently after treatment for a hemorrhagic pericardial effusion due to a supratherapeutic INR. This admission was marked by bilateral pleural effusions and crackles on exam, initially raising concern for pneumonia or recurrent cardiac tamponade. A bedside echocardiogram ruled out pericardial fluid, and clinical stability without fever led to a diagnosis of fluid overload secondary to ESRD. She received dialysis, which improved her symptoms, and antibiotics were discontinued due to lack of infectious signs. No medication changes were made. She was discharged to extended care with instructions for fluid and sodium restriction, daily weight monitoring, and continuation of home therapies including anticoagulation, insulin, and BiPAP.
